messages:
alice: heads-up — the latest python/ts SDK PR will start sending the new route-negotiation header by default next week. we need a plan to avoid breaking internal proxies.

sam: ugh timing. which header? route-neg or x-route-hint?

alice: route-negotiation:v1 (JSON blob). current proxies expect x-route-hint. idea is to ship a client-side shim that emits both headers for a grace period, then flip.

gina: +1 for shim but console UX needs a way to show which orgs/apps are on the new header so support can triage. telemetry event would help.

yuri: agree. we should also avoid spamming telemetry — emit a lightweight event header_migration=1 and sample at 1% by default. make it configurable via console.

sam: what about an env var so infra teams can opt out immediately if needed?

alice: proposal: default shim_mode=dual for 30 days, add env var REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_ROUTE_SHIM=1 to opt out, console rollout tile to toggle "graceful-mode" per org, telemetry sampled 1% (configurable), plus a tiny migration script in devex to rewrite calls for old proxies.

sam: can we put a deprecation warning log in the SDK when shim disabled? that will surface owners in SRE dashboards.

gina: console tile should show: list of orgs still sending x-route-hint, estimated % traffic, and a link to migration docs + rollout timeline. also add a checkbox to auto-enable shim for new apps.

deploy-bot: Deployed python-sdk v2.3.1-shim-flag to canary (us-west) :rocket:

alice: thanks — i'll draft the docs PR and the migration script. tagging @platform for router-side compatibility checks and fallback policies.

sam: i'll run a quick smoke on our internal proxy tomorrow. if no surprises, ship the 30-day window.
